item.title: A little bit of good news...
item.description:
Bruce Fischer, the husband of Nebraska U.S. Senator Deb Fischer and who went viral last year for refusing to shake the hand of U.S. Vice President Kamala Harris, has died. Senator Fischer confirmed the death of her husband on Monday in a statement, revealing he died on Sunday while “doing what he loved most, spending time outdoors.” “Our family is heartbroken by his passing, but we find comfort in the life we shared with him,” said Fischer. “Above all, Bruce was a loving husband, a devoted father and grandfather, a man of faith, and a rancher. We sincerely appreciate the prayers, kindness, and support extended to our family during this difficult time.” Fischer, 75, was re-elected for a third term in the 2024 election. After Deb Fischer was sworn into office by Vice President Harris on Jan. 3, 2025, Bruce Fischer, standing right beside his wife, ignored Harris’ attempt to shake his hand in congratulations.
Bruce Fischer instead looked down, nodded, and said, “Thank you.” He refused to make any eye or physical contact with America’s first female, first Black woman and first South Asian vice president. Harris, who appeared taken aback by the snub, simply smiled and said, “You sure?” The controversial moment led Harris’ husband, former Second Gentleman Doug Emhoff, to reportedly confront Bruce Fischer for the perceived disrespect of his wife. During a ceremonial tea event at the White House ahead of President Donald Trump’s inauguration last year, Bruce Fischer attempted to shake Emoff’s hand. Emhoff refused the gesture, considering the snub against Harris just days earlier. “Why would you try to shake my hand when you wouldn’t shake my wife’s hand?” Emhoff said to Fischer, according to CNN. The outlet reports that after the confrontation, Fischer eventually came back to Emhoff to apologize. The two had a “cordial” conversation in which “tempers had cooled” and they eventually began talking about golf and other topics.
Sources: https://x.com/AntiTrumpCanada/status/2125203298307235916 Husband of Republican senator who refused Kamala Harris’ handshake dies https://thegrio.com/2026/11/23/bruce-fischer-dies-kamala-harris-handshake-snub/

item.title: GovBrief Today #663
item.description: Kilmar Abrego Garcia landed in Spain tonight, 20 months after Donald Trump's government illegally deported him to El Salvador. The government admitted its error to the Supreme Court, which ordered it to help bring him home from the Terrorism Confinement Center. Government lawyers called that impossible, and El Salvador's president said he didn't have the power. Trump said he could, and didn't. When Abrego Garcia finally came home, it was to face smuggling charges based on a 2022 traffic stop. Nobody charged him with anything at the time, and a judge threw the case out before trial. Then the government kept trying to send him to Africa. He agreed to go to Costa Rica, Costa Rica agreed to take him, and in June Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told senators, "we'll be happy to send him." As he left for Spain, Mullin's department said it was "delighted" Abrego Garcia was gone and that he will never be allowed back into the country where his wife and son are citizens. Our Zoom In feature has every step in his journey to be freed from the government's mistake. On February 1, 2025, I typed a list of nine things I never imagined a government doing in one day and sent it to my family. I've sent one every night since: 10,091 stories over 663 straight nights, free and without ads. Add your email address at govbrief.today and I'll send it to you too. item.title: Donald Trump Jr under investigation over 'suspiciously well-timed' investments
item.description:
Democrats have announced an investigation into one of the US president's sons over what they describe as "suspiciously well-timed government favours". The probe will examine if Trump Jr used his influence to steer federal contracts towards Hadrian Automation, Juul Labs, Polymarket, and GrabAGun. Trump Jr's firm 1789 Capital had a stake in all four of those companies.
